name: National Air and Space Museum
unique: The Wright Flyer, the Spirit of St. Louis, a moon rock you can touch and the actual command module from Apollo 11, all free.
buzz: The renovated galleries are stunning; timed passes vanish, so reserve at 10am exactly 30 days out.

name: National Gallery of Art
unique: A free national collection with the only Leonardo in the Americas, a Calder mobile in the rotunda and an East Building by I.M. Pei that is as good as anything hanging in it.
buzz: The West Building for old masters and the East for modern; the sculpture garden in summer and the moving walkway between buildings are the local route.

name: National Museum of African American History and Culture
unique: A bronze and glass corona on the Mall that takes you from the slave trade in the basement to music and sports on the top floors, with Emmett Till's casket and a slave ship timber.
buzz: The history galleries below ground are the reason to reserve a pass; people say three hours is not enough and the top floors are the relief after the descent.

name: Library of Congress
unique: The Main Reading Room and the Great Hall: mosaics, murals and marble, plus Jefferson's own library and a Gutenberg Bible behind glass.
buzz: The free timed-entry pass is the easiest win in DC; the reading room overlook is the photo. Don't miss the tunnel to the Capitol.

name: Lincoln Memorial at Dawn
unique: The marble chamber above the reflecting pool, where the Gettysburg Address is carved on one wall and the view back to the Capitol lines up with the sunrise.
buzz: Go before seven and you will have the steps almost alone; the chamber under the memorial and the view from the back are the parts people miss.

name: Kennedy Center Millennium Stage
company: John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts
unique: A free performance every single evening at 6pm, from gospel choirs to chamber music to experimental theater, in a marble hall over the Potomac.
buzz: Locals treat it as the best free cultural secret in the city; the rooftop terrace at sunset is its own attraction.

name: National Archives
unique: The rotunda holding the Declaration of Independence, the Constitution and the Bill of Rights in dim cases, with a mural of the founders above them.
buzz: The documents are faded and the room is dark and it still lands; go at opening to avoid the school groups.

name: Cherry Blossom Festival
unique: Three thousand cherry trees gifted by Tokyo in 1912 detonate into a pink ring around the Tidal Basin for ten days, with a parade and kite festival.
buzz: Peak bloom is unpredictable; locals check the NPS forecast daily and go at dawn. Parking is impossible, take Metro.

name: National Museum of American History
unique: The flag that inspired the anthem, Julia Child's kitchen, the Greensboro lunch counter and Dorothy's ruby slippers in one free building on the Mall.
buzz: The Star Spangled Banner room is the quiet moment and the transportation hall is for children; the building is easier to enter than the newer museums.

name: Phillips Collection
unique: The first museum of modern art in the country, in a Dupont Circle house with Renoirs, Rothkos and a Rothko room designed for quiet looking.
buzz: The Rothko room is the reason people return and the house scale makes it intimate; it is small and the admission is modest.

name: National Zoo
unique: Giant pandas when the loan agreement allows, a free zoo in Rock Creek Park, and the compact Asia Trail that puts you feet from a sloth bear.
buzz: Free entry makes it a DC staple; the pandas drive the crowds and the hill is steeper than it looks. Go at opening.

name: Ford's Theatre
unique: The working theater where Lincoln was shot, with the presidential box preserved and a museum in the basement, still staging plays at night.
buzz: The ranger talk in the box is worth waiting for and the Petersen House across the street is included; timed tickets go fast in spring.

name: National Museum of the American Indian
unique: A curvilinear limestone building on the Mall with a collection organized by tribe rather than chronology, and a cafeteria of Native dishes from across the hemisphere.
buzz: The cafeteria is a destination on its own and the galleries reward slow reading; the building's form and the landscape design are part of the exhibit.

name: National Portrait Gallery
unique: Portraits of every president and the people who changed the country, including the Lansdowne portrait of Washington, in a former patent office building.
buzz: The presidential gallery and the modern portraits are the route and the courtyard is the quiet break; it is free and connected to the American Art Museum.

name: US National Arboretum
unique: Four hundred and forty six acres inside the city with the National Bonsai and Penjing Museum, a grove of state trees and the columns of the old Capitol standing in a meadow.
buzz: The bonsai museum is the surprise and free; the Capitol columns are the photograph and the azalea collection peaks in late April.

name: Frederick Douglass National Historic Site
unique: Cedar Hill, the house Douglass bought after the war, with his library, his desk and a view over the Anacostia and the Capitol.
buzz: The ranger tour is the only way in and the view from the porch is half the story; the site is in a neighborhood most visitors never see.

name: Hillwood Estate
unique: The estate of the Post cereal heiress, with a collection of Russian imperial art including Faberge eggs, and a Japanese garden and French parterre.
buzz: The Faberge collection is the reason art people come and the gardens are the quiet afternoon; it is off the tourist track and never crowded.

name: International Spy Museum
unique: Tradecraft you can touch: a real Enigma, disguise stations, listening devices and the stories of spies who defected, lied and disappeared.
buzz: The interactive undercover assignment is a hit with teens; adults want more artifacts and less queue. Book a timed slot.

name: Kenilworth Aquatic Gardens
unique: The only national park devoted to aquatic plants, with ponds of lotus and water lilies on the Anacostia and a boardwalk through a tidal marsh.
buzz: The lotus bloom in July is the event and photographers arrive at dawn; the park is in a quiet part of the city and feels overlooked.

name: 9:30 Club
unique: A 1,200 capacity club that has broken more bands than any room its size in the country, with a balcony that puts you almost on the stage.
buzz: The sound is consistently good and the sightlines from the balcony are the secret; shows sell out and doors are early.

name: ARTECHOUSE
unique: A subterranean digital art space under the Mall where projectors turn the walls and floor into a moving environment, with a different artist each season.
buzz: The scale is impressive in a small room; shows change often so check what is running. Good rainy day option.

name: Eastern Market
unique: A brick market house from 1873 where butchers and a blueberry buckwheat stand still work the hall, with a weekend flea market and a crab cake counter outside.
buzz: The market hall is best on Saturday morning and the flea is behind it; the blueberry pancakes at Market Lunch are the standing order.

name: Georgetown C&O Canal
unique: A cobblestone towpath along the canal from Georgetown to Great Falls, with lock houses, a mule drawn boat and herons in the middle of the city.
buzz: The first three miles from Georgetown are flat and shaded and the mule boat runs Wednesday to Sunday; the path is gravel and busy on weekends.

name: Maine Avenue Fish Market
unique: The oldest continuously operating open air fish market in the country, a row of barges on the Washington Channel selling crabs, oysters and fried fish to order.
buzz: The crabs are sold by the dozen and the fried shrimp box is the cheap lunch; it is outdoors, cash friendly and best at lunchtime.

name: Rock Creek Park
unique: Eighteen hundred acres of wooded valley through the middle of the city, with a creek, a mill, a planetarium and a trail network that connects to the Potomac.
buzz: Locals run the trail on weekday mornings and the Peirce Mill grinding days are the family draw; the parkway closes to cars on weekends in summer.

name: Supreme Court
company: Supreme Court of the United States
unique: The marble temple with a courtroom you can sit in, a spiral staircase and exhibits on the cases that shaped the country.
buzz: The courtroom and the self guided tour are free and quick; oral argument days need a line and the building is across from the Capitol.

name: Theodore Roosevelt Island
unique: A wooded island in the Potomac reached by a footbridge, with a memorial plaza to Roosevelt in a clearing and trails through swamp and upland forest.
buzz: The island feels nothing like the city and the memorial is usually empty; the boardwalk on the north end is the birding spot.

name: Nationals Park
unique: A ballpark on the Anacostia with a center field plaza, a presidents race in the fourth inning and a view of the Capitol from the upper deck.
buzz: The presidents race is the tradition and the standing room areas are good; tickets are cheap on weeknights and the metro stops at the gate.

name: Tidal Basin Paddle Boats
company: DC Department of Parks and Recreation
unique: A paddle boat on the Tidal Basin with the Jefferson Memorial on one side and the cherry trees on the other, from the water.
buzz: The view from the water is different from the shore and the boats are cheap; the basin is shallow and the queue is long in cherry blossom week.

name: Union Market
unique: A 1931 wholesale market turned food hall with butchers, a tortilleria, a oyster counter and a rotating set of pop ups, north of Capitol Hill.
buzz: The food stalls change often and the oyster bar and the tacos are the standards; it is busy on weekends and easier on weekdays.
